uncovered_reasons.note: Mixed string + number concatenation; the numeric operand (guarded via performance.now number type guard) is known, but the compiler does not strength-reduce a + whose other operand is a string literal (number-to-string conversion stays generic).

Property is a prototype accessor (Object.defineProperty getter/setter on Z80.prototype); accessor loads/stores always invoke the accessor and are never strength-reduced to a data slot. Attempted: instance shape guard (Z80ObjHot3), full prototype-shape binding on Z80.prototype + prototype-shape guard, and a number type guard on the loaded value — dryrun reported all no-effect / killed by the accessor read.

(Setter sites also run during reset while the receiver shape is still being constructed.)

Method inherited from a prototype (Z80.prototype or Memory.prototype), not an own data property. The call itself is optimized via a closure type guard, but the property load stays a generic prototype lookup: prototype-shape guards were tried exhaustively (Z80Proto/MemoryProto shapes, prototype bindings, guards with prototype shape on the instance) and this build never specializes inherited property loads, instead killing the shape fact.
